{{Short description|German computational neuroscientist}}
'''Gregor Schöner''' (born 1958 in Sindelfingen<ref name=":0">{{cite web|access-date=2022-09-11|date=2017-09-19|language=de|publisher=Ruhr Universität Bochum|title=Vita Gregor Schöner|url=https://dynamicfieldtheory.org/upload/file/1505813537_005822fff11bb41cb03a/vita.pdf|website=Dynamic Field Theory}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>) is a German [[Computational neuroscience|computational neuroscientist]]. He is a professor of the theory of [[Cognitive Systems|cognitive systems]] at the [[Ruhr University Bochum]] and the director of the Institute for Neuroinformatics.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|access-date=2022-09-11|language=de|publisher=Ruhr-Universität Bochum|title=Organizational Structure of the Institute|url=https://www.ini.rub.de/the_institute/organizational_structure/|website=Institut für Neuroinformatik}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Life and work ==

From 1983 to 1985, Gregor Schöner studied physics and mathematics at [[Saarland University]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1985, he received his PhD in [[theoretical physics]] from the [[University of Stuttgart]] under [[Hermann Haken|Herrmann Haken]]. For the next four years, he devoted himself to applications of the theory of stochastic dynamical systems to the coordination of biological motion under [[J. A. Scott Kelso]] at [[Florida Atlantic University]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-09-11|language=en|publisher=Intelligent Servosystems Laboratory, Pamela L. White|title=ISR CED Lecture {{!}} Bio Schoener|url=https://isr.umd.edu/Labs/ISL/CDS_Lecs/Bios/schoener_bio.html}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> From 1989 to 1994, he led a research group for the first time at the Institute of Neuroinformatics at Ruhr University in Bochum. In that time, he and his group extended the application of dynamical systems to models of perception, motion, and autonomous robotics. After a six-year stay at the Centre de Recherche en Neurosciences Cognitives in [[Marseille]], Gregor Schöner returned to the institute in 2001. He took over its leadership in 2003, succeeding [[Christoph von der Malsburg]],<ref name=":0" /> and has remained in this position until today.<ref name=":1" /> Since September 2022, he has been the chairman of the Society for Cognitive Science in Germany.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-09-11|language=de|publisher=Gesellschaft für Kognitionswissenschaft e.V.|title=Vorstand|url=https://www.gk-ev.de/?page_id=55|website=Gesellschaft für Kognitionswissenschaft ev}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

Gregor Schöner and his research group are known for the scientific development, applications, and software packages on Dynamic Field Theory (DFT). DFT provides a neurally plausible framework for the [[Mathematical Modeling|mathematical modeling]] of human cognition according to the theories of [[embodied cognition]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-09-11|language=en|publisher=Oxford University Press|title=Dynamic Thinking: A Primer on Dynamic Field Theory|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/10360?login=false|website=Oxford Academic}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> The theory builds upon the continuous [[attractor network]]s models of Hugh R. Wilson and [[Jack D. Cowan]] (the "[[Wilson–Cowan model|Wilson-Cowan model"]])<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wilson |first1=H. R. |last2=Cowan |first2=J. D. |date=1973 |title=A mathematical theory of the functional dynamics of cortical and thalamic nervous tissue |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00288786 |journal=Kybernetik |language=en |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=55–80 |doi=10.1007/BF00288786 |pmid=4767470 |s2cid=292546 |issn=0023-5946|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[Shun'ichi Amari]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Amari |first=Shun-ichi |date=1977 |title=Dynamics of pattern formation in lateral-inhibition type neural fields |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00337259 |journal=Biological Cybernetics |language=en |volume=27 |issue=2 |pages=77–87 |doi=10.1007/BF00337259 |pmid=911931 |s2cid=2811608 |issn=0340-1200|url-access=subscription }}</ref> (the "neural field model"), which describe the interaction between excitatory and inhibitory coupled populations of [[cortical neurons]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Schöner |first1=Gregor |title=Dynamic thinking: a primer on dynamic field theory |last2=Spencer |first2=John P. |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-930056-3 |series=Oxford series in developmental cognitive neuroscience |location=Oxford New York Auckland Cape Town Dar es Salaam Hong Kong Karachi Kuala Lumpur Madrid Melbourne Mexico City Nairobi New Delhi Shanghai Tapei Toronto}}</ref> Schöner's research group publishes on [[visual search]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Grieben |first1=Raul |last2=Tekülve |first2=Jan |last3=Zibner |first3=Stephan K. U. |last4=Lins |first4=Jonas |last5=Schneegans |first5=Sebastian |last6=Schöner |first6=Gregor |date=2020 |title=Scene memory and spatial inhibition in visual search: A neural dynamic process model and new experimental evidence |journal=Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics |language=en |volume=82 |issue=2 |pages=775–798 |doi=10.3758/s13414-019-01898-y |issn=1943-3921 |pmc=7246253 |pmid=32048181}}</ref> spatial and relational language,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Richter |first1=Matthis |last2=Lins |first2=Jonas |last3=Schneegans |first3=Sebastian |last4=Sandamirskaya |first4=Yulia |last5=Schöner |first5=Gregor |date=2014 |title=Autonomous Neural Dynamics to Test Hypotheses in a Model of Spatial Language |url=https://escholarship.org/content/qt5014s78t/qt5014s78t.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society |volume=36 |issue=36 |pages=2847–2852}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sabinasz |first1=Daniel |last2=Schöner |first2=Gregor |date=2023 |title=A Neural Dynamic Model Perceptually Grounds Nested Noun Phrases |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/tops.12630 |journal=Topics in Cognitive Science |language=en |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=274–289 |doi=10.1111/tops.12630 |pmid=36303455 |s2cid=251245352 |issn=1756-8757|doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[autonomous robotics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Schöner |first1=G. |last2=Dose |first2=M. |last3=Engels |first3=C. |date=1995 |title=Dynamics of behavior: Theory and applications for autonomous robot architectures |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0921889095000496 |journal=Robotics and Autonomous Systems |language=en |volume=16 |issue=2–4 |pages=213–245 |doi=10.1016/0921-8890(95)00049-6|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
